main_topics.reason: The opening question and the first several turns were about the link between stressful work weeks and flares, and what to do about it.
The user asked what to do on a Tuesday morning with back-to-back meetings, and the bot answered over several turns.
The user was skeptical, then interested, and asked where to find hypnotherapy; it made up a long stretch of the conversation.
The user asked in a follow-up whether loperamide can be taken before symptoms appear, and the bot explained timing and dosing.
The user raised their heavy coffee use on stressful days and acknowledged it was counterproductive.
The user said urgency is disruptive during meetings, which frames the acute need.
The user said their doctor only said to eat more fiber, and the bot gave a script for the next visit.
The user asked in one turn whether to involve their doctor or try things alone.
The user asked for a combined plan, and the bot laid out long-term and acute layers.

output.summary: A user with IBS asked what could help when flares (diarrhea, cramping, urgency) strike during stressful work weeks. The bot explained the gut-brain link and covered gut-directed hypnotherapy, CBT, antispasmodics, tactical loperamide and cutting back caffeine, then gave a plan and advice on when to involve the doctor. The user said it was more useful than their doctor's fiber advice and that they had real things to try.
